words.meaning: A second check when you sign in, like a code sent to your phone.
A private, locked connection to the work network over the internet.
Single sign-on. One sign-in that opens many work apps.
A step-by-step guide for a common task.
The company list of staff, with names, titles and phone numbers.
You can look at it, but you cannot change anything.
Chief financial officer. The leader in charge of a company's money.
Human resources. The team that handles hiring, staff records and people leaving.
Extra power to install apps, change settings and manage other accounts.
A saved copy of files, kept so they can be brought back if lost.
The settings, files and apps kept for one user on a computer or phone.
Paid permission for one person to use a piece of software.
Calling a person back on the phone number already on file, to check who they are.
A website where people send requests or see their records.
A small program that runs a list of steps by itself.
The second level of support staff. They take the harder problems.
An outside company that sells goods or services to a business.
A record a system keeps of what happened and when.
To erase all data on a device. A remote wipe does it over the internet.
The steps to close a worker's accounts and access when they leave.
An automatic email reply that says the person is away.
Notes that tell the next worker what was done and what is left.
The name part of an email or web address, like example.com.
A tool that moves unwanted bulk email out of the inbox.
A named list of users. Everyone in it gets the same access.
